newsitem.title: DUBAI: Emirate awards power plant order to US firm.
newsitem.headline: Emirate awards power plant order to US firm.

text.p: The emirate of Ajman has awarded a contract to an American firm to set up and manage a power station, a United Arab Emirates newspaper said over the weekend.

The project, aimed at helping meet Ajman's increasing power needs, is the first such programme in the oil-rich United Arab Emirates, the newspaper al-Khaleej quoted Ajman Crown Prince Sheikh Ammar bin Humaid bin Rashid al-Nuaimi as saying.
He gave no further details and did not say when the deal was signed. Officials were not immediately available for comment.

Ammar also said the northern emirate, which plans to expand its free trade zone, now home to 100 local and international companies, was studying an offer for a water desalination project from an international firm.
"The government is still studying its feasibility."

Abu Dhabi, capital of the seven-member United Arab Emirates, late last year set up a committee to oversee the privatisation of its water and electricity services. It also appointed consultants to study the feasibility of privatisation.
Like its Gulf Arab neighbours, the UAE wants to reduce reliance on the dominant public sector and give private investors a bigger role.
The water and electiricity sector have taken the lion's share of United Arab Emirates investments -- accounting for over 7 billion dirhams ($1.9 billion) in three years.

Water consumption in the emirates, where the population is growing at around 4 percent annually, was expected to rise to almost 606 million gallons a day by the year 2015 from a curent 232.5 million. In 1995, the emirates raised power rates by 33 percent, but electricity and water are still heavily subsidised.
